sample_rows.title: Officer Coverage
sample_rows.description:
•	TfL sets road categories within the TLRN and defines minimum enforcement frequencies (e.g. Cat 1 - 2 officers, twice daily).
•	Supplier must deploy officers to meet these minimums.
•	TfL assesses the Supplier's coverage (rather than the supplier reporting on it) using 'mystery shopper' style audits of supplier deployment at key locations.

sample_rows.title: Deployed Officer Hours
sample_rows.description:
•	Supplier submits yearly, monthly, and weekly deployment plans detailing officer numbers and total deployed hours to meet TfL's enforcement frequencies; TfL approves these in advance.
•	Supplier measures and reports actual officer numbers and deployed hours against the plans each period using roster data, GPS, etc.

sample_rows.title: PCN Error Rate
sample_rows.description: TfL sets a threshold for the number or % of PCNs cancelled due to officer error or insufficient information each period. Supplier must ensure the threshold is not breached.

sample_rows.rationale:
Need for additional works, services or supplies by the original contractor/concessionaire: The existing Service Provider has a detailed technical understanding of this programme, including familiarity with the programme objectives, data sets, internal governance and stakeholder landscape.
The initial tender procedure only produced a single compliant bid, which indicates limited market capacity or appetite to deliver this specialist work.
Securing a technically comparable supplier at this stage is unlikely without incurring additional cost, delay, and programme risk. Were one to be identified they would then require a significant mobilisation period in order to to review historic work, reconstruct the analytical approach, recreate project baselines, and re establish stakeholder and governance alignment. These activities would largely duplicate work already completed and paid for under the existing contract. As a result, a change of contractor at this point would result in significant inconvenience and material duplication of cost without delivering additional value.

sample_rows.tender_description:
NHS Wales Shared Service Partnership on behalf of Public Health Wales NHS Trust wish to inform the market that due to the Covid-19, global pandemic they are awarding a contract for the provision of Sexually Transmitted Infection testing kits, postal envelopes and any other associated consumables to continue an online service for self-sampling.
NHS Wales Trust have been running an online service for self-sampling for STI’s since 2018 and will eventually expand to an All Wales Agreement.
Public Health Wales laboratories previously supported the expansion which has been agreed by Welsh Government. However, during the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic, Public Health Wales laboratories were suspended for the use of STI sampling to support the national testing campaign.
Therefore in order to enable the provision of STI testing and to continue the patient online service for self-sampling, Public Health Wales awarded a contract to HSL Pathology Lab to continue the testing in private laboratories during the height of the pandemic.
However, now that the cases associated with the Covid-19 pandemic are rising further and the Public Health Wales laboratories are overwhelmed with Covid-19 testing, the service are awarding an extension contract to HSL Pathology Lab. The external provider are currently able to deal with 15000 requests a week between now and end of March 2021 in order to ensure continuation of sexual health testing.

Background information:
In shaping a healthier and more active future for our residents. It is now necessary for the Council to procure an Operating Partner to operate the Council owned Facilities within the former Copeland and Allerdale Borough Council areas with effect from the 1st of April 2026. It is intended that the procurement and resultant contract will be procured in such a way to allow flexibility over the term of the contract, for instance building in the possibility to include the Carlisle contract when it ends in December 2032.
The Facilities in scope include:
Former Allerdale Area – contract ends 31st March 2026
• Workington Leisure Centre;
• Cockermouth Leisure Centre;
• Keswick Leisure Centre (only the gym is open / pool is closed); and
• The Wave, Maryport.
Former Copeland Area – contract ends 31st March 2026
• Whitehaven Leisure Centre;
• Copeland Pool and fitness centre; and
• Cleator Moor Activity Centre.
In addition to the above facilities, the Council is due to commence construction of a new Facility in Millom in 2025. This facility will also form part of the Facilities that will be included in the scope of the Leisure Operating Contract.
For clarity, the Council owned Facilities operated by Better Leisure within the Carlisle leisure contract are not in scope from the commencement in April 2026 but could be become integrated at the end of the current contract period, include:- Former Carlisle Area - contract ends 6th December 2032
• The Sands Centre;
• The Sheepmount; and
• Bitts Park Tennis Courts.

TfL invites suppliers to participate in this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise to help shape an upcoming procurement opportunity. This is a valuable chance to engage with us early, gain insight into our requirements, and contribute your expertise.
The engagement process consists of three key steps:
1. Registering Interest - Suppliers who wish to participate should express their interest by emailing MichaelWilliams1@tfl.gov.uk . The deadline for registering interest is Friday 14th March 2025.
2. Information Sharing - Once the registration window closes, we will issue a concise, one-page requirements document to all interested suppliers. This will outline key details of the procurement and may include specific questions to help us understand market capabilities and potential approaches.
3. Follow-Up 1:1s - Based on the responses received, we will identify suppliers who align with the requirement, which includes provision of workforce for on-street parking enforcement patrols.
The supplier must have experience of providing on-street parking enforcement services in a metropolitan area. We are not interested in a technology-only solution which does not provide on-street parking enforcement patrols.
Up to three suppliers will be invited to a 1:1 one-hour MS Teams meeting planned to take place between Monday 17th to Friday 28th March 2025. The discussions will provide an opportunity for TfL to explore the market in greater depth, discuss your responses to TfL's questions, and consider the approach to overall market. Please note that generic feedback on the 1:1s will be issued to all interested suppliers.
We are exploring various options including a single contract or multiple contracts covering separate areas of London.
Summary
We encourage all interested suppliers, regardless of size, to take part in this process. Your insights and expertise will be invaluable in shaping our approach.
If you have any questions about the process, please don't hesitate to get in touch with MichaelWilliams1@tfl.gov.uk. We look forward to hearing from you.

There is no action required of tenderers at this stage. The Authority will make an assessment of the Economic & Financial Standing of each tenderer (and any consortia or reliance partners) using the Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) 'Failure Score' indicator and the following process:
Step 1: A D&B 'Failure Score' of 50 or above will result in a PASS.
Step 2: If the tenderer (or any consortium or reliance partner) scores below 50, then the audited financial accounts of the tenderer (or consortia or reliance partner) will be used to conduct an assessment of the risk of business failure. If this assessment identifies an unacceptable risk then the tenderer (or consortia or reliance partner) will fail this assessment
Financial Accounts For Question 4B6 of the SPD, bidders may elect to provide their audited financial accounts for the last three financial years. There must be no qualification or contra-indication from any evidence provided in support of the tenderer's Economic and Financial Standing.
